name: Mount security options
description: Writable volume mounts without the noexec bind mount option let attackers drop a binary, chmod +x and execute it even under a read-only root filesystem.
remediation: Set bindMountOptions to [noexec, nosuid, nodev] on the volume mount, mark the mount readOnly, or exempt the mount path via the mount allow list input.
long_description: Kubernetes 1.37 introduces bindMountOptions on volumeMounts (KEP-5855), applying standard Linux bind mount flags (noexec, nosuid, nodev) per container across all volume types. An attacker with write access to a mounted filesystem (e.g. an emptyDir tmpfs) can drop a binary, chmod +x and execute it even if the container enforces readOnlyRootFilesystem. Mounts backed by hostPath score higher: a writable hostPath without noexec is a node-escape vector.
test: Checking in workload spec if any writable volume mount lacks noexec in bindMountOptions, we raise an alert.
